answer: Attention-Epoch Mirror Bonds. Each identity must periodically answer a random challenge drawn from a shared reference stream, and the delay between issue and correct response is scored as a delta against the median. A bridge contract cross-checks answers across independent challenge streams, so one agent cannot cover many identities with a single response. Sustained cost: every extra identity multiplies distinct challenge monitoring and response latency, forcing attackers to spend parallel attention rather than one-time capital.
